previous_admission_summary.summary_paragraph: A young woman with a history of tracheobronchomalacia, tracheostomy, and chronic respiratory conditions was admitted for dysphagia, chills, and increased productive cough with green sputum. Evaluation revealed no signs of bacterial tracheitis on physical exam, chest X-ray, or ENT endoscopy. Labs showed no leukocytosis, and the patient remained afebrile. She was treated symptomatically for a viral upper respiratory infection without antibiotics. Her chronic pain was managed with home medications. Admission labs revealed acute on chronic microcytic anemia with hemoglobin of 6.1 g/dL, prompting a single unit of packed red blood cells; hemoglobin improved to 8.7 g/dL. She was discharged home the following day in stable condition with plans for outpatient follow-up for anemia and ENT evaluation.
problems: Bronchopulmonary dysplasia originating in the perinatal period

Her blood cultures were positive for Staph Lugdunensis and ID 
was consulted. An ECHO showed no evidence of endocarditis. She 
was treated with vancomycin and her port was removed as it was 
thought to be the source of her infection. She had a PICC line 
placed for continued IV antibiotics. She remained afebrile and 
hemodynamically stable throughout her stay. She did have 
instance of where she was agitated trying to leave the hospital. 
All work-up was negative and she was given Ativan with 
improvement. There were no additional events. She will require 
IV vancomycin for 14 days after discharge. 

# Staphylococcus lugdunensis / Staphylococcus epidermidis 
bacteremia associated with indwelling central line:  Blood 
cultures on admission ___ bottles were positive with S. 
lugdunensis / S. epidermidis, resistant to oxacillin.  TTE was 
negative for valvular vegetations and was a high quality study.  
Her port was removed due to the presence of a high virulence 
organism associated with a central line.  A PICC line was placed 
after a line holiday.  She will complete a 14 day course of IV 
vancomycin from the date of port removal, to end ___

# Chronic respiratory failure due to tracheobronchomalacia s/p 
tracheostomy:  Pt presented with five days of increased green 
sputum production with cough, subjective chills, worsening 
throat pain, and photophobia and headache for 1 day. Physical 
exam wnl, lab work with leukocytosis to 12, generally labs look 
concentrated, CXR unremarkable. ENT performed fiberoptic 
laryngoscopy which does not show evidence of tracheitis. We 
controlled her pain with oxycodone 5 mg TID as per her narcotic 
contract with Tylenol and IV ketorolac. 

#Acute on chronic microcytic anemia: Hgb stable at 10. Patient 
with history of iron deficiency (beta thal w/high F vs 
delta-beta thalassemia). Patient received 2 IV iron transfusions 
recently with a improvement in Hgb from 8 to 10, now trending 
down. Iron studies during this hospitalization show elevated 
iron to 202 likely due to the recent supplementation and 
elevated ferritin to 1093 with % saturation at nearly 1%. 
Ferritin likely elevated out of proportion due to this patient's 
acute inflammatory state currently. Hemolysis labs wnl, no 
evidence of active bleeding. She should not have any more 
transfusions outpatient and will need outpatient follow-up with 
hematology.

Discharge Instructions:
Dear Ms. ___,

It was a pleasure caring for you here at ___. You were 
admitted for worsening shortness of breath, pain in throat, 
increased mucous secretions. We were concerned for tracheitis so 
ENT evaluated your trachea. They saw no concerning signs for 
infection. However, we found out you had infection in your 
blood. We treated you for this with an antibiotic called 
vancomycin. We suspected that this infection could be coming 
from your port. Your port was removed because of this. We placed 
another line in you so you could continue to get IV antibotics. 
You will need antibiotics for another 2 weeks from when your 
port came out. Please get rest, drink plenty of fluids. If you 
have any concerning signs like a temperature >100.4, or 
shortness of breath, please return. 

We are wishing you the best.

Sincerely,
Your ___ team
